title: Operational request, travel, and vendor playbook
author: Maya Thompson
summary: Unified playbook for request fulfillment, change and access requests, travel and expense rules, vendor onboarding and procurement templates. Provides stepwise procedures, approval matrix, example templates and escalation paths for cross-functional teams.
body:
Purpose and scope

This playbook collects company-wide operational rules and repeatable procedures for: access and permissions changes, change management for production systems, data handling for procurement and travel artifacts, procurement and expense approvals, vendor onboarding and ongoing vendor lifecycle, and travel policy enforcement. It is intended for requestors, approvers, finance, legal, security, and ops teams.

Audience
- Requestors (employees initiating requests)
- Approvers (managers, finance, security, legal)
- Operational owners (IT, SRE, Procurement)
- People-ops and finance teams executing reimbursements and vendor payments

Key principles
- Least privilege: access granted for the minimum duration and scope required.
- Separation of duties: procurement, legal review, and payments must be separated from request initiation when cost or risk thresholds are exceeded.
- Single source of truth: all requests go through the Request Fulfillment system (internal RFC portal).
- Auditability: decisions, approvals, and artifacts must be stored with the request record for the retention period defined below.

1) Roles & ownership (high level)
- Requestor: initiates the request, provides justification and attachments.
- Manager (level-1 approver): verifies business justification and budget owner consent.
- Finance reviewer (level-2 approver for >$1,000): verifies budget availability and expense code.
- Legal reviewer (applies to contracts, STAs, data handling, >$10k or cross-border): reviews terms & data residency.
- Security reviewer (applies to access changes and vendor systems): completes risk checklist and third-party questionnaire.
- Procurement operations: executes purchase orders and vendor setup.
- IT/Access team: performs access changes, implements network/VPN rules.

2) Approval matrix (summary)
| Request type | Threshold | Level-1 approver | Level-2 approver | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Standard access (non-privileged) | any | Manager | - | auto-granted after manager approval, expires 90 days |
| Elevated access (DB/admin) | any | Manager | Security | Requires approval and audit logging |
| Procurement - low cost | <$1,000 | Manager | Finance (optional) | Direct PO via self-serve catalog |
| Procurement - medium | $1,000–$10,000 | Manager | Finance | Finance approves cost center and payment method |
| Procurement - high | >$10,000 | Manager | Legal + Finance + Procurement | Legal reviews contract terms; security reviews data risk |
| Travel - domestic | any | Manager | Finance (reimbursement) | Per travel policy limits |
| Travel - international | any | Manager | Legal + Finance | Passport/visa assistance and cross-border approvals |

3) Request-to-fulfillment procedure (canonical steps)
1. Create request in RFC portal using the appropriate template (access-change, procurement, travel). Attach required artifacts (quote, SOW, vendor MSA draft, travel itinerary).
2. Manager reviews within 3 business days. If approved, request auto-routes to next approver(s). If denied, requestor receives feedback and the record is closed.
3. Finance and/or Legal reviewers have 5 business days for review on medium/high requests. Security completes technical and risk review within 5 business days for access or vendor system requests.
4. For vendor and contract requests: Procurement operations generates PO or SOW, negotiates payment terms, and initiates vendor setup (W-9 / tax form / bank details) in Vendor Portal.
5. IT/Access executes changes only after approvals are recorded. Change windows must be scheduled for production-impacting changes and follow the change-management runbook (see related pages).
6. After fulfillment, the requestor confirms completion and provides acceptance evidence when applicable. Finance marks invoices for payment after acceptance or upon invoice terms.

SLA targets
- Manager review: 3 business days
- Finance/Legal/Security: 5 business days for medium/high risk items
- Procurement PO issuance: 7 business days after all approvals
- Access execution for non-prod: 2 business days after approvals; for prod elevated access, schedule within approved change window

4) Access & permissions procedure (examples and templates)
- Access requests must include: justification, requested resources (service name, role, datasets), duration, and data handling requirements.
- Temporary elevated access: maximum 30 days unless extension is approved by Security and Manager.
- Access revocation: Owners must confirm access removal 2 business days after task completion or on expiration.

Access request template (YAML example):

---
request_type: access_change
requestor: name@example.com
system: analytics-cluster-prod
roles_requested: [read_queries, temp_admin]
justification: "Investigate analytics job failures for ticket #12345"
duration_days: 7
data_classification: confidential
attachments: ["ticket-12345.log"]
---

5) Change management notes
- All production-impacting changes must be logged in the Change Calendar and have a linked RFC.
- Emergency changes: must be documented immediately after execution, include root cause, and follow the incident-to-change process for retroactive approval.
- Rollback plan required for any change with potential user-facing impact.

Change checklist (quick):
- Impact analysis completed
- Backout/rollback steps documented
- Monitoring and alerting updated
- Owner and on-call notified
- Post-change validation steps defined

6) Procurement, vendor onboarding and vendor lifecycle
Vendor risk tiers and required artifacts:
| Vendor Tier | Examples | Required documents | Risk reviewers | Payment flow |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 - Strategic | Cloud providers, core infra vendors | MSA, SOC2, DPA, SLAs | Legal + Security + Procurement | Contract + PO via purchasing card or invoice |
| Tier 2 - Operational | SaaS tools with limited data | MSA or click-through terms, security questionnaire | Procurement + Security | PO or card |
| Tier 3 - Low risk | One-off purchases | Invoice, W-9 | Procurement | Card |

Vendor onboarding steps (canonical):
1. Initiate vendor request in RFC portal with vendor name, contact, expected spend, data access needs and attachments.
2. Procurement validates vendor identity and tax forms.
3. Security runs third-party questionnaire and requests SOC/penetration test evidence when Tier 1/2.
4. Legal reviews MSA/DPA and negotiates terms.
5. Procurement creates PO and vendor record in ERP, finance sets payment terms.
6. Vendor is added to allowed-vendors list and systems with least-privilege access.

Ongoing vendor reviews:
- Quarterly reviews for Tier 1 vendors (contract KPIs, SLO adherence, security posture).
- Annual reassessment for Tier 2.
- Decommissioning steps include data return/wipe confirmation and certificate revocation where applicable.

7) Travel policy and expense rules (digest)
- Booking: employees must use the company travel portal for flights and hotels for reimbursement and cost tracking. Exceptions require manager pre-approval.
- Per diem and limits: domestic meals up to $75/day; international vary by region (see travel portal). Airfare must be economy coach; upgrades require pre-approval and a business justification.
- Corporate card usage: preferred for travel and vendor purchases when available; reimbursement requires itemized receipts and business purpose.
- Expense submission: within 10 business days of return or purchase; late submissions may be denied or require manager justification.

Travel approval flow:
1. Requestor submits itinerary + cost estimate.
2. Manager approves business need.
3. Finance verifies budget and issues corporate card or reimbursement estimate.
4. Legal reviews if travel involves restricted countries or sensitive customer visits.

Expense template (table):
| Field | Required? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Date | Yes | Date of expense |
| Merchant | Yes | Itemized vendor name |
| Amount | Yes | Currency and amount |
| Business purpose | Yes | Link to meeting invite/ticket |
| Receipt | Yes | Upload PDF or image |
| Expense code | Yes | Finance cost center |

8) Data management for procurement and travel artifacts
- Data classification: invoices, tax forms, and contracts are internal-confidential. Vendor access to customer or production data requires Tier 1 controls and a DPA.
- Retention: financial documents retained according to Finance retention schedule (minimum 7 years for tax documents). Travel records retained for 3 years. Access request logs retained for 2 years.
- Encryption: vendor PII and bank details must be stored encrypted at rest with access restricted to procurement and finance roles.

9) Escalation and exception process
- If approvals exceed expected SLA or a dispute arises, escalate to the Request Fulfillment guild (ops-request-guild@redwood.example.com) and include the request ID.
- Policy exceptions require documented justification, a risk owner, and a timeboxed approval from the C-level sponsor (Finance or Security depending on scope).

10) Templates and attachments (appendix)
- Access-request template (see above YAML).
- Vendor onboarding checklist (CSV/checkbox): vendor details, tax docs, security evidence, legal sign-off, procurement record ID.
- Travel pre-approval form (PDF template link): fields for business purpose, estimated cost, manager sign-off.
- Expense submission CSV example: date, merchant, amount, purpose, receipt_link, cost_center.

Operational best practices and notes
- Reuse vendor agreements when possible to reduce negotiation overhead.
- Consolidate travel bookings to take advantage of negotiated hotel rates.
- Automate reminders for access expirations and vendor review windows.
- Maintain a published vendor inventory with data access tiers and contact points.
